fact: DNEC says more than 20 million NINA have been attributed to Malians through the CTDEC, from a biometric file built from civil status.

The government says President Goita officially launched the new sovereign Mali Kura Biométrie system replacing the old RAVEC file on 13 February 2024, after the old system's blockage from April 2023 had slowed biometric ID card production.
The document names NINA, the national identification number, as the unique identifier of each voter, with a biometric civil-status database behind the lists.

L'Essor describes a biometric civil-status database holding photos and fingerprints and a national identification number (NINA), the definitive NINA being assigned by the service managing that database.
Aujourd'hui-Mali reports that the secure biometric national identity card is issued to Malian citizens at home and in consulates, with the data held in Mali Biométrie.

The Aujourd'hui-Mali article says the CNIBS, instituted by decree of 3 November 2022, is starting to be made operational with enrolment stations being installed in Bamako police and gendarmerie posts.
The article says subscribers hold the NINA national identity number and a biometric card derived from it, and that a ministry official says people must identify biometrically and each hold a NINA.

Mali's Ministry of Territorial Administration says full biometric enrolment functions resumed on 14 February 2024 under Mali Kura Biometrie, the RAVEC system, with national NINA numbers issued from the RAVEC database.
Mali Tribune reports subscribers' SIMs were registered using biometric data and the number from their NINA card, so the NINA card and number are in use.
